RAJYARAJYA   SABHA SABHA
—————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December  17, 2004/ Agrahayana 26, 1926 (Saka)
—————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
72
Violation of labour lawsViolation of labour laws
*241. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Ministry of Railways is
aware of the gross violation of labour laws,
pertaining to minimum wages, right to form
union etc. and anti-workers activities by
Hindustan Construction Company (HCC),
the contractor engaged in construction work
in Banihal in Doda district of Jammu and
Kashmir;
(b) if so, the action taken by the Ministry
of Railways, as principal employer, to stop
repression directly or indirectly by HCC
on the above contractor's workers
comprising migrant, dalit and minorities; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Loss due to increase in price of steelLoss due to increase in price of steel
†*242. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Railways are making any
loss due to frequent increase in the price
of steel;
(b) if so, the details of the loss;
(c) whether Government are trying to
find out substitute of steel;
(d) if so, what are the details in this
regard; and
(e) whether Government are
contemplating to manufacture aluminium
wagons in place of steel wagons?
New technologies/systems to checkNew technologies/systems to check
the loss of foodgrainsthe loss of foodgrains
*243. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have assigned the task of evolving new
technologies/systems to check the loss of
foodgrains and post-crop production to
some Central Research Organisations;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether any headway has been
made so far?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

CGHS Homoeopathic dispensariesCGHS Homoeopathic dispensaries
*244. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of new CGHS
Homoeopathic dispensaries opened in
Delhi since 1987 till date, year-wise and
location-wise;
(b) if not, the specific reasons therefor;
(c) the number of new CGHS Allopathic
dispensaries opened in Delhi since 1987
till date, year-wise and location-wise; and
(d) the necessary steps being taken by
Government to set up new CGHS
Homoeopathic dispensaries in comparison
to Allopathic dispensaries in Delhi?
Joint study by AIIMS and World BankJoint study by AIIMS and World Bank
*245. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
a study jointly carried out by AIIMS and
World Bank, 69 per cent of the injections
given at Government hospitals are unsafe
and contribute in spreading diseases like
AIDS, Hepatitis and Malaria;
(b) if so, the other revelations made by
the above study; and
(c) the action that has been
contemplated by Government on the
outcome of the study?
Incentives for Rabi production targetsIncentives for Rabi production targets
*246. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to provide incentives to States for meeting
Rabi targets;
(b) if so, the steps being taken and
incentives that are being provided to States
to meet Rabi targets;
(c) whether any concrete programme of
action has been prepared to meet the
shortage of Kharif production which was
affected due to delay in monsoon;
(d) whether despite sluggish Kharif
production, foodgrain output in 2004 has
been up; and
(e) if so, whether Government are
confident of meeting foodgrain shortage so
that the demand of foodgrains by States
are fully met?
Landscape railway stationsLandscape railway stations
*247. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
landscape railway stations in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the benefits likely to accrue from
the proposal?
Infant deathsInfant deaths
*248. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India ranks
first in the total number of child deaths,
with 2.4 million dying before the age of
five, whereas China with a higher
population base, ranks third with 7,84,000
child deaths;
(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor,
indicating figures of neonatal mortality rate

List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 17, 2004/Agrahayana 26, 1926 (Saka)

(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food and
Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing Industries;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions —155
Milk production project by NDDB in
Uttaranchal
1590. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether some milk production
projects have been undertaken in the joint
sector with co-operative milk federations
of different States by NDDB;
(b) if so, whether any such project has
been started in Uttaranchal;
(c) whether Government have received
any proposal to undertake some of such
projects in that State; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Funds for agricultural marketing
1591. DR. AKHILESH DAS: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have launched
a scheme to make available funds for
developing and strengthening agricultural
marketing only for such States as have
made certain policy changes towards
reforms;
(b) if so, the nature and details of the
policy changes required for the State
Governments to qualify for the aid under
this scheme; and
(c) the extent of aid extended there-
under to different States, so far?
Timing of Kathgodam and New Delhi
Sampark Kranti Express
1592. SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO
JOSHI: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
passengers from hilly areas of Uttaranchal
are left stranded and are unable to use the
Sampark Kranti Express between
Kathgodam and Delhi, as it arrives and
departs from Kathgodam at 10.45 P.M. and
8.50 A.M. respectively, and the State
Government has banned public transport
on hills during night;
(b) if so, whether Government would
change the departure timing of the train to
4 P.M. from Kathgodam and 9 A.M. from
Delhi; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

351
(c) whether Government propose a link
train from Ramnagar be connected with this
train similar to the Ranikhet Express to
benefit people of Garhwal?
Subsidy vis-a-vis interest of farmers
†1593. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn towards the statement made by
the Planning Commission wherein it has
been said "The key for the development of
Agriculture is to increase the capital
investment and not to give subsidy";
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that developed
western countries are giving annual subsidy
in terms of billions of dollars to their
agricultural producers; and
(d) if so, what arrangements will be
made to safeguard the interests of Indian
farmers in international market?
Rice scam
1594. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the present status of rice scam in
Karnataka;
(b) the quantity of rice involved and
misused which was meant for Food for
Work Programme;
(c) whether an enquiry by CBI is being
ordered/contemplated; and
(d) whether similar scams occurred in
other States in the country; if so, the details
thereof?
Income of small and marginal farmers
1595. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the debt burden on poor and
marginal farmers is increasing and sourcing
of their income decreasing day by day in
the country;
(b) if so, the details of average income
annually of poor and marginal farmers in
each State/UT as on date and also of annual
debt;
(c) whether Government propose to
write off agricultural loan at least up to
10,000 rupees; if so, the details thereof; if
not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) what schemes Government propose
to give financial relief to poor farmers in
the country in 2005-06?
Drought assistance to Andhra Pradesh
1596. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of various schemes and
facilities provided to farmers affected by
continuous drought;
(b) the details of budget released,
scheme-wise for 2001-2002, 2002-2003
and 2003-2004, district-wise and Mandal-
wise in Andhra Pradesh, to save the farmers
from worst crisis, due to continuous
drought; and
(c) if not, the reasons for not releasing
any budget or any special package schemes,
so far?
Agricultural growth
1597. SHRI MANOJ BHATTA-
CHARYA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
